target_customer: Independent coffee shops and small cafes in the United States
problem: Coffee shop owners juggle many separate tools for ordering, payments, scheduling, marketing and payroll, and general restaurant POS systems are not built around coffee workflows.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payments and hardware (pricing starts at about $160 a month per the January 2026 Sprudge piece)
product_category: Vertical POS and operating system for coffee shops

founders.name: Jack Pawlik
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO with no background. A Stripe newsroom story says he spoke to coffee shop owners and heard they wanted one app to run the business.

founders.name: Avery Durrant
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and co-CEO in the TechCrunch article of 2024-04-24. The YC page lists only Pawlik.

competitors.name: Odeko
competitors.what: Inventory and supply software for brick and mortar coffee retailers, merged with Cloosiv to add mobile ordering
competitors.traction_then: Launched 2019 in New York; customers named include George Howell Coffee, La Colombe and Gregory's
competitors.funding_then: Combined $28M raised with Cloosiv after a $12M round announced 2020-08-18

competitors.name: Cloosiv
competitors.what: Mobile ordering app for independent coffee shops, founded 2017 in Charlotte
competitors.traction_then: Hundreds of retail users across the US as of late 2019
competitors.funding_then: $1M seed in 2019 reported by TechCrunch, then merged into Odeko in August 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: POS, scheduling and mobile ordering with payments integration are standard engineering for a small team, with hardware and payments compliance as the harder parts.

defensibility.rationale: General POS vendors could copy features, but a shop that runs ordering, payroll and scheduling on one system faces real switching costs once adopted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company's own comparison pages and the 2024 TechCrunch headline position Dripos against Square and Toast. No evidence found that either built a coffee-specific product or bought Dripos.

market_need_then: The company says there are about 100,000 US cafes and that owners used 10 or more tools per shop. Dated 2020 demand evidence was not found beyond the YC listing.

branding.domain_note: Operates on dripos.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: New logo introduced in the January 2026 rebrand (details not described by the source)
identity.visual_style: Design-led identity aimed at the coffee community per the 2026 rebrand coverage
identity.voice_and_tone: Built by people who run coffee shops; craft and community language

branding.brand_signature: Counter Talk, the company's own coffee industry publication launched with the 2026 rebrand

rebrands.to: Dripos (new logo, visual identity and website)
rebrands.why: CEO says it reflects commitment to the craft and the community; marks a new chapter after the Series A

branding.community_and_virality: Company staff are called Drip Drops per search results (single mention, unverified); trade press such as Sprudge covered the rebrand.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage (Sprudge, Daily Coffee News) and a company publication show niche brand investment, but no evidence of broad consumer recognition.

outcome_analysis: Dripos grew from a Summer 2020 YC company into a vertical coffee shop operating system that claims over 3% of US coffee shops and raised an $11M Series A led by Base10 in April 2024. Its wedge was a coffee-specific all-in-one product against general POS vendors, and press reported fast growth in locations. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff reports were found as of the research date.
notes: TechCrunch states total raised of $17.3M, implying about $6.3M of earlier funding that the article does not itemize. Seedtable lists a $5.0M seed in March 2022 (aggregator only, unverified, not recorded as a round). Founding year 2019 per TechCrunch and Sprudge; one aggregator says 2020. Square and Toast are named by the company and YC page but no source dated near 2020 was found, so they are not in the competitor list. Dated outcome searches found nothing about acquisition or layoffs.
